newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat warning precedes Israel-Egypt summit.
newsitem.headline: Arafat warning precedes Israel-Egypt summit.

text.p: Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat urged Israel before an Israel-Egypt summit on Tuesday to freeze Jewish settlements and warned of disaster unless peacemaking resumed.

"The problem isn't building for Palestinians, rather halting the settlements," Arafat told Israel's daily Haaretz ahead of a meeting between Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Egypt's President Hosni Mubarak.
Arafat said he hoped the summit, at the Egyptian Red Sea resort of Sharm el-Sheikh, would succeed in reviving Israeli-Palestinian negotiations deadlocked for more than two months.

Israel, which plunged peace moves into crisis in March when it broke ground on a Jewish settlement of 6,500 homes in Arab East Jerusalem, last week approved the building of 3,400 homes for Arabs opposite the site.

Arafat's remarks appeared to pour cold water on a possible face-saving proposal published by the Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper to have Israel complete the housing infrastructure for the Jews and then the Arabs before building housing for both.
Arafat forecast a "disaster" unless Israel and his PLO made progress in peacemaking. Asked if he feared a war, he said: "Not only war, but confusion in all of the Middle East."
His adviser Ahmed Tibi said he knew of no compromise proposals likely to emerge from the summit, the first between Mubarak and Netanyahu in nearly three months.

"Israel is still not ready to commit to stop the settlements and so long as it is unwilling to commit to stop the settlements and stop the construction on Jabal Abu Ghneim, the situation will remain unchanged," Tibi told Israeli army radio.
The Jewish settlement is at a site Palestinians call Jabal Abu Ghneim and Israelis call Har Homa.

Palestinians want an end to settlement expansion, saying it pre-empts final peace talks at which Jerusalem's fate is to be negotiated. Palestinians want East Jerusalem, captured and annexed by Israel in 1967, as capital of a future state.
